prompt: Convert a non-negative int to its binary string recursively using division and remainder by 2 -- without Integer.toBinaryString. Complete the toBinary method, then run the tests.
explanation: Dividing by 2 chops off the lowest binary digit, and n % 2 is exactly that digit -- so the binary form of n is the binary form of n / 2 with the last bit appended. The recursion bottoms out when n is 0 or 1, which are their own binary representations. Handling 0 and 1 together in one base case (n < 2) also makes toBinary(0) return "0" while larger numbers never produce leading zeros, because the recursion stops before dividing down to zero.
hints: Base case: when n is 0 or 1, its binary form is just itself -- return String.valueOf(n).
Recursive case: the bits of n / 2 come first, then the single bit n % 2.
Return toBinary(n / 2) + (n % 2); concatenating the int n % 2 onto a String turns it into "0" or "1" automatically.
